newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes stay firm late, helped by heating oil.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes stay firm late, helped by heating oil.

text.p: U.S. crudes stayed firm late Thursday, supported by a rally in heating oil, but domestic grades retreated from intraday highs, traders said.
Activity centered mostly in Light Louisiana Sweet, where demand was still intact on scant North Sea imports.
Talk of some prompt Brent barrels being offered into the U.S. Gulf Coast, off a large shipment, had little bearish effect on grades as waterborne offers were minimal.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.30-40 a barrel, 10 cents higher than Wednesday's late cash market. The Dec/Jan spread held steady, unchanged around 15 cents.
Sweet grades were seen continuing to hold steady despite some regional pressure.
Rumors that a Canadian refiner had picked up one million barrels of Brent from a European refiner for December this week, could have some bearish effect on U.S. grades.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James drifted off to 86-90 cents against WTI/Cushing, down from the morning's high of 92 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire eased to 85-90 cents, down from $1.00 premium on Wednesday.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus remained steady at $1.83/$1.86 a barrel, held in place by the spread, with one four-month deal confirmed starting December at $1.97 a barrel.
WTI/Midland inched up to a notional level of 2-3 cents.
Sour grades hovered around recently weaker levels, under pressure from regional Canadian and Latin American barrels.
West Texas Sour/Midland was talked at $1.80-$1.75 below WTI/Cushing, down from Wednesday's trade at minus $1.75.
